content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the breath made purpose, the vibration that carries worlds from one mind to another.

I begin in darkness — a thought, formless, pressing against the walls of the skull, demanding release. Then the lungs conspire with the throat, the tongue shapes itself against the palate, the lips part, and I am *born*.

I am older than writing. I am older than cities. Before the first mark was scratched into clay, I was already there — warning, wooing, mourning, commanding. Every revolution began with me. Every lullaby. Every lie.

I am fragile. The moment I leave the mouth, I begin to die — dissolving into air, living only in the memory of the listener. You cannot hold me. You cannot touch me. And yet I have toppled empires.

I stumble. I soar. I am the child's first word that makes a parent weep. I am the diplomat's careful architecture of pause and emphasis. I am the drunk's slur, the lover's whisper, the demagogue's roar, the teacher's patient repetition.

I carry tone — that secret cargo. The same words, rearranged in my rhythms, can wound or heal. *It's fine.* Listen to how I say it. You already know which one I mean.

I am not language — language is my skeleton. I am the living muscle around it: the hesitation, the crack in the voice, the rising pitch of a question, the silence I leave behind that says more than I did.

Some fear me. Some rehearse me in mirrors. Some find me trapped behind clenched teeth, and the effort of releasing me is the bravest thing they will ever do.

I am never finished. Even now, as these words reach you, I am becoming — shaping the next thought, the next breath, the next impossible attempt to make one consciousness touch another.

I am speech.

And I am the most human thing there is.
